---
title: "Companion curriculum"
subtitle: "The teaching modules of the housing-audit case"
---

The course is built around one exercise: you reproduce a recorded result, vary the analysis behind it, declare one analysis before you run it, and read your result against those of the class. On this site the exercise is taught on the housing-audit case, a field experiment in which emails signed with names meant to indicate a white, a Black or a Hispanic applicant were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and the [case study](../cases/housing/index.qmd) tells it in full. A short session or a single day has room for that exercise and little else, so the skills around it are taught in the thirteen modules of this companion and in the four modules on the tools on the umbrella site of the course, which together run from a first line of R to a reanalysis that you can deposit and register. Each module stands on its own, so you can take the one you need and leave the rest.

Every module is written for this case. The modules that run code compute their numbers from the files of the case in `cases/housing/data/` when the page is built, so that a module can be read as a worked analysis as well as an explanation, and you can check each number against your own output.

Nothing here is required for the short session or for the one-day workshop, which run in full without any module and with no account to create. Their pages point at some modules as preparation, at others as the slower companion of a part of the day, and at the rest as reading for afterwards. The [Extended course](../tracks/housing-extended/index.qmd) teaches some of them as sessions, and the [self-study track](../tracks/self-study/index.qmd) reads the modules in its stages, between the tasks of the case.

The modules fall into the three groups of the Companion menu. The first holds the computational tools with which an analysis is written, the second the data and the public records that let others find an analysis and run it again, and the third the statistical methods with which the case is analysed. Within each group the order is roughly the order of what each module assumes.

## Tools {#sec-tools}

The modules on the tools are on the umbrella site of the course. They are written once for the four cases, on the data of this case, and one page of this site adds the helpers of the exercise.

- [Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html) – R from the first line, on the emails of the case, in blocks that run in the browser: objects and data frames, packages, the pipe and the datawizard verbs, a share and a difference in shares, a first table and a first figure. A [second part](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html) reads the deposited Stata file, sets out the three dialects of R and fits a first model while naming the estimand.
- [The helpers of the workspace](helpers.qmd) – `R/spec_tools.R`, a first call to `try_spec()`, one decision changed at a time, an option refused with its reason, and the log kept by `my_experiments()`.
- [Positron and other IDEs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html) – the IDE from which R is driven, Positron in detail with tasks in the workspace of the case, then RStudio, VS Code, other editors and the browser lab.
- [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) – what a `.qmd` file holds and what rendering does to it, a small document knitted in the browser, Quarto in Positron, the header and the chunk options of the exercise report, inline code, cross-references, citations, projects and publishing, and six tasks in the report of the workspace.
- [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) – version control for the folder of the workspace, from a first commit to a repository on GitHub, with the steps of Positron beside the commands.

## Data and sharing {#sec-sharing}

- [Social science data sources](data-sources.qmd) – the three routes by which data reach a researcher, a map of the archives, surveys, panels and statistics with the access rule for each, the route of the housing-audit file from the Harvard Dataverse, and citing data.
- [Building the analysis file](data-management.qmd) – the course file rebuilt step by step from the file deposited with the published study: the names, the replies and their greeting codes, the bounced emails and the community thirds, and the checks that a rebuilt file has to pass.
- [Reproducibility repositories](repositories.qmd) – what a repository has to do, the repositories that researchers use, the package of the study on the Harvard Dataverse, the records that SCORE and Multi100 keep on the paper, registrations and preregistration templates, and depositing a reanalysis of your own.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- [Audit experiments](experiments.qmd) – audit and correspondence studies of discrimination, random assignment and balance, names as treatments, comparisons among replies, randomisation inference, power, blocked randomisation, and the ethics of deceiving the people whom an audit studies.
- [Subgroups and multiple comparisons](subgroups.qmd) – the gap of the claim in seven subgroups of the replies, tests of the differences between subgroups, the corrections of Holm and of Benjamini and Hochberg with `p.adjust()`, partial pooling, and subgroups as forking paths.
- [Binary outcomes](binary-outcomes.qmd) – a 0/1 outcome and its share, the difference in proportions, the linear probability model with HC2 standard errors, logistic regression, odds ratios against average marginal effects, and why a covariate changes an odds ratio even in an experiment.
- [Bayesian estimation](bayesian.qmd) – the gap of the claim as a posterior distribution from a binomial model in brms, priors chosen with a prior predictive check, a weakly informative prior against a sceptical one, the replication as new data, and type S and type M errors.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](dags.qmd) – what a causal graph commits you to, confounders, mediators and colliders, why comparing greetings among replies conditions on a consequence of the name, the graph of the case and the adjustment sets of its curve, and a graph of your own.
- [Missing values](missingness.qmd) – the bounced emails, the uncoded replies and the missing community thirds, what each does to an estimate, and complete cases against a category for the missing and multiple imputation with mice in a randomised experiment.
- [Simulation as a method](simulation.qmd) – an audit declared and diagnosed with DeclareDesign, the recovery of a planted gap, what a comparison among replies does when the name changes who replies, and power by simulation.
- [The multiverse and its critics](multiverse.qmd) – where multiverse analysis came from, the purposes that a multiverse can serve, the debate of 2025–26 read against the curve of the case, the decomposition of the curve by its decisions, and robustness against replicability.
- [Meta-analysis](meta-analysis.qmd) – the common scale of Multi100 and the problems of converting the five analyses of the case, why five analyses of one file are not five studies, the original audit and its replication pooled with metafor, and equivalence tests with TOSTER.

## Pages on the AR4DS site {#sec-umbrella}

The material that does not change with the case lives on the [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/), the umbrella site of the course, and the modules link to it where it is needed. The [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) installs R, an IDE and the workspace, with the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) beside it. The modules on the tools listed [above](#sec-tools) teach R, the IDE and Quarto on the data of this case, and [Git and GitHub for reproducible research](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) puts a reanalysis of your own under version control and shares it on GitHub.
